questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: Which of the following is an associative form of social interaction?

options.A: Competition
options.B: Conflict

questions.explanation: Associative forms of social interaction include cooperation, accommodation and assimilation; dissociative forms include competition and conflict.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: Which of the following is a dissociative form of social interaction?

options.A: Cooperation
options.B: Accommodation

questions.explanation: Dissociative forms of social interaction include competition and conflict; associative forms include cooperation, accommodation and assimilation.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a major social institution according to the notes?

options.A: Family
options.B: Education

questions.explanation: The family, marriage, kinship, education, religion, economy, polity or government, and law are commonly treated as major social institutions. A sports club is an organisation, not a major social institution.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: Which of the following is a form of polygamy?

options.A: Monogamy
options.B: Polygyny

questions.explanation: Polygyny is a form of polygamy in which one man has more than one wife. Polyandry is another form of polygamy.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: Which of the following is a form of polyandry?

options.A: Fraternal polyandry
options.B: Polygyny

questions.explanation: Fraternal polyandry is a form of polyandry in which a woman is married to two or more brothers.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: A mother's brother's child is an example of which type of cousin?

options.A: Parallel cousin
options.B: Cross-cousin

questions.explanation: A cross-cousin is the child of a parent's opposite-sex sibling, such as a mother's brother's child or a father's sister's child.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: A father's brother's child is an example of which type of cousin?

options.A: Cross-cousin
options.B: Parallel cousin

questions.explanation: A parallel cousin is the child of a parent's same-sex sibling, such as a father's brother's child or a mother's sister's child.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: A university is an example of which type of group?

options.A: Primary group
options.B: Secondary group

questions.explanation: A university can function as a secondary group, which is generally larger and more formal with impersonal, specialised and goal-oriented relationships.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: A family is an example of which type of group?

options.A: Secondary group
options.B: Primary group

questions.explanation: Family, close friendship groups and intimate neighbourhood groups are common examples of primary groups.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: Which of the following is the earliest agent of socialisation?

options.A: School
options.B: Peer group

questions.explanation: Family usually provides the earliest sustained interaction through which children learn language, basic norms, values, habits and social roles.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of secondary socialisation?

options.A: Learning language from parents
options.B: Learning basic norms within the family
options.C: Learning roles and expectations in schools and workplaces

questions.explanation: Secondary socialisation is the learning of roles and expectations in settings beyond the early family environment, such as schools, workplaces and peer groups.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of ascribed status?

options.A: Becoming a doctor through education
options.B: Being born into a particular caste
options.C: Achieving a promotion through hard work

questions.explanation: Ascribed status is a social position assigned to an individual largely at birth or without personal choice, such as being born into a particular caste.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of achieved status?

options.A: Being born into a particular family
options.B: Being born into a particular caste
options.C: Becoming a doctor through education and effort
options.D: Being born in a particular village

questions.explanation: Achieved status is a social position acquired through an individual's actions, efforts, qualifications or accomplishments, such as becoming a doctor through education and effort.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: Which of the following is a characteristic of caste?

options.A: Achieved status only
options.B: Free mobility between groups

questions.explanation: Common characteristics historically associated with caste include birth-based membership and endogamy, along with hierarchy, hereditary occupations, social restrictions and ideas of purity and pollution.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: Which of the following is a characteristic of class?

options.A: Strictly birth-based membership
options.B: Endogamy as a defining feature
options.C: Close relation to economic position and greater mobility

questions.explanation: Class is more closely related to economic position and can allow greater mobility, unlike caste which is traditionally birth-based and endogamous.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: A person moving from a clerical job to a managerial job is an example of which type of mobility?

options.A: Horizontal mobility
options.B: Vertical mobility

questions.explanation: Movement from a clerical job to a managerial job involves a change in social rank and is an example of vertical mobility.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: A person changing from one clerical job to another clerical job at a comparable level is an example of which type of mobility?

options.A: Vertical mobility
options.B: Horizontal mobility

questions.explanation: Horizontal mobility is movement between positions of broadly similar social rank, such as changing jobs at a comparable level.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: Which of the following is a push factor of migration?

options.A: Higher wages at the destination
options.B: Better education at the destination
options.C: Unemployment in the place of origin

questions.explanation: Push factors are conditions that encourage people to leave an area, such as unemployment, poverty, landlessness, conflict, environmental stress or inadequate services.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: Which of the following is a pull factor of migration?

options.A: Poverty in the place of origin
options.B: Landlessness in the place of origin
options.D: Environmental stress in the place of origin

questions.explanation: Pull factors are conditions that attract people to a destination, such as jobs, education, healthcare, higher wages, infrastructure and perceived opportunities.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of subsistence agriculture?

options.A: Farming mainly for sale in markets
options.B: Farming primarily to meet the consumption needs of the farmer's household
options.C: Farming using high-yielding varieties for export

questions.explanation: Subsistence agriculture is farming primarily intended to meet the consumption needs of the farmer's household rather than to produce mainly for sale.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of commercial agriculture?

options.A: Farming primarily to meet household consumption needs
options.B: Farming mainly to produce crops or livestock for sale in markets

questions.explanation: Commercial agriculture is farming mainly intended to produce crops or livestock for sale in markets.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: The spread of a new technology from one society to another is an example of which process?

options.A: Cultural lag
options.B: Cultural diffusion

questions.explanation: Cultural diffusion is the spread of cultural traits, ideas, practices or technologies from one group or society to another.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: The delay in adjusting laws to new technological developments is an example of which concept?

options.A: Cultural diffusion
options.B: Cultural lag

questions.explanation: Cultural lag is the delay in the adjustment of one part of culture, often non-material culture such as laws or values, to changes in another part, often technology.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: A movement seeking to change particular laws while retaining the broader social system is an example of which type of movement?

options.A: Revolutionary movement
options.B: Reform movement

questions.explanation: A reform movement seeks to change particular institutions, laws or practices while generally retaining the broader social system.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: A movement seeking fundamental and rapid transformation of the political, economic or social order is an example of which type of movement?

options.A: Reform movement
options.B: Revolutionary movement

questions.explanation: A revolutionary movement seeks fundamental and often rapid transformation of the political, economic or social order.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a social norm?

options.A: A personal opinion about a film
options.B: A shared expectation that people should greet elders respectfully

questions.explanation: A social norm is a shared rule or expectation that guides behaviour in a particular society or group, such as greeting elders respectfully.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a social value?

options.A: A personal preference for a particular colour
options.B: A shared belief that education is important in society

questions.explanation: A social value is a shared belief about what is desirable, important or worthwhile in a society, such as the importance of education.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: A couple living with the husband's parents after marriage is an example of which residence pattern?

options.A: Matrilocal residence
options.B: Patrilocal residence

questions.explanation: Patrilocal residence is a post-marital residence pattern in which the couple lives with or near the husband's family.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: A couple living with the wife's parents after marriage is an example of which residence pattern?

options.A: Patrilocal residence
options.B: Matrilocal residence

questions.explanation: Matrilocal residence is a post-marital residence pattern in which the couple lives with or near the wife's family.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: A couple establishing a separate household after marriage is an example of which residence pattern?

options.A: Patrilocal residence
options.B: Matrilocal residence

questions.explanation: Neolocal residence is a post-marital pattern in which the couple establishes a separate household.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: Marriage within one's own caste is an example of which practice?

options.A: Exogamy
options.B: Endogamy

questions.explanation: Endogamy is the rule or practice of marrying within a specified social group, such as a caste, community or religious group.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: Marriage outside one's own caste is an example of which practice?

options.A: Endogamy
options.B: Exogamy

questions.explanation: Exogamy is the rule or practice of marrying outside a specified social group.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: A woman marrying into a family of higher social status is an example of which practice?

options.A: Hypogamy
options.B: Hypergamy

questions.explanation: Hypergamy is marriage into a group or status considered higher than one's own, according to a particular social hierarchy.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: A woman marrying into a family of lower social status is an example of which practice?

options.A: Hypergamy
options.B: Hypogamy

questions.explanation: Hypogamy is marriage into a group or status considered lower than one's own, according to a particular social hierarchy.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: A village is an example of which type of community?

options.A: Urban community
options.B: Rural community

questions.explanation: A rural community is a community situated in a countryside or village setting, often characterised by lower population density and a significant role for agriculture or allied activities.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: A city is an example of which type of community?

options.A: Rural community
options.B: Urban community

questions.explanation: An urban community is a community located in a town or city, typically characterised by higher population density, occupational diversity and complex institutions.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: People sharing a characteristic such as age or gender but not interacting with each other form which type of collection?

options.A: Social group
options.B: Social category

questions.explanation: A social category is a classification of people who share a characteristic, even if they do not interact or identify as a group.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: A temporary gathering of people at a railway station is an example of which type of collection?

options.A: Social group
options.B: Social category

questions.explanation: A crowd is a temporary gathering of people in a common physical setting, often responding to a shared event or stimulus.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: A collection of people in the same place or situation who may not share lasting interaction or group identity is called what?

options.A: Social group
options.B: Social aggregate

questions.explanation: A social aggregate is a collection of people in the same place or situation who may not share lasting interaction or group identity.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: A person learning the values and behaviour of a profession they plan to enter is an example of which type of socialisation?

options.A: Primary socialisation
options.B: Secondary socialisation

questions.explanation: Anticipatory socialisation is learning the values, norms and behaviour associated with a role or group that a person expects to enter.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: A person in a rehabilitation programme learning new norms and behaviour patterns is an example of which process?

options.A: Primary socialisation
options.B: Secondary socialisation

questions.explanation: Resocialisation is the process of replacing or substantially modifying previously learned norms, values and behaviour patterns.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: A lower-status caste adopting the rituals and practices of a higher-status caste is an example of which process?

options.A: Westernisation
options.B: Sanskritisation

questions.explanation: Sanskritisation is the process through which a lower-status caste or group seeks upward social mobility by adopting practices, rituals, values or lifestyles associated with a locally dominant or higher-status group.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: Adoption of English education and Western institutions in India is an example of which process?

options.A: Sanskritisation
options.B: Westernisation

questions.explanation: Westernisation refers to changes in Indian society associated with prolonged contact with Western institutions, technology, education, ideas and ways of life.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: A system in which status is assigned largely by birth and movement between positions is restricted is called what?

options.A: Open system of stratification
options.B: Closed system of stratification

questions.explanation: A closed system restricts movement between social positions and assigns status largely by birth or inherited membership.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: A system that permits comparatively greater movement between social positions through education and achievement is called what?

options.A: Closed system of stratification
options.B: Open system of stratification

questions.explanation: An open system permits comparatively greater movement between social positions, often through education, occupation, income or achievement.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: A child from a working-class family becoming a doctor is an example of which type of mobility?

options.A: Downward mobility
options.B: Upward mobility

questions.explanation: Upward mobility is movement to a higher social or economic position, such as a child from a working-class family becoming a doctor.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: A person losing their job and moving to a lower economic position is an example of which type of mobility?

options.A: Upward mobility
options.B: Downward mobility

questions.explanation: Downward mobility is movement to a lower social or economic position.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: A son having a higher occupational status than his father is an example of which type of mobility?

options.A: Intragenerational mobility
options.B: Intergenerational mobility

questions.explanation: Intergenerational mobility is a change in social position between different generations of a family, such as between parents and children.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: A person changing their occupation and improving their social position during their own lifetime is an example of which type of mobility?

options.A: Intergenerational mobility
options.B: Intragenerational mobility

questions.explanation: Intragenerational mobility is a change in an individual's social position during that person's own lifetime.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: Industrialisation creating many new occupational positions that enable people to move between class positions is an example of which type of mobility?

options.A: Exchange mobility
options.B: Structural mobility

questions.explanation: Structural mobility occurs when broad economic or social changes alter the distribution of positions, enabling or requiring many people to move between occupational or class positions.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: A government programme deliberately designed to improve literacy is an example of what?

options.A: Unplanned social change
options.B: Planned social change

questions.explanation: Planned social change is deliberate transformation pursued through policies, programmes, legislation or organised collective action.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: A natural disaster causing widespread displacement and social transformation is an example of what?

options.A: Planned social change
options.B: Unplanned social change

questions.explanation: Unplanned social change occurs without a coordinated intention to produce the resulting transformation, often through unintended consequences or external events.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: A farmer owning less than 1 hectare of land is classified as what in Indian agricultural statistics?

options.A: Small farmer
options.B: Marginal farmer

questions.explanation: A marginal operational holding is generally one below 1 hectare.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: A farmer owning 1 hectare or more but below 2 hectares is classified as what in Indian agricultural statistics?

options.A: Marginal farmer
options.B: Small farmer

questions.explanation: A small operational holding is generally 1 hectare or more but below 2 hectares.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a tier of the Panchayati Raj system?

options.A: Gram Panchayat
options.B: Panchayat Samiti

questions.explanation: The three commonly recognised tiers of Panchayati Raj are Gram Panchayat at village level, Panchayat Samiti or an equivalent body at intermediate level, and Zilla Parishad at district level. Municipal Corporation is an urban local body.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: The movement of people from large cities to smaller towns or rural areas is called what?

options.A: Urbanisation
options.B: Suburbanisation

questions.explanation: Counter-urbanisation is the movement of people or activities from large urban centres to smaller towns or rural areas.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: The expansion of population and activities from a central city into surrounding areas is called what?

options.A: Counter-urbanisation
options.B: Suburbanisation

questions.explanation: Suburbanisation is the expansion of population and activities from a central city into surrounding suburban areas.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a characteristic of society?

options.A: It is abstract
options.B: It is dynamic
options.C: It is based on social relationships

questions.explanation: Society is abstract, dynamic, relatively continuous, interdependent, based on social relationships, characterised by similarities and differences, and regulated by norms and institutions. It is not purely biological.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a latent function of education?

options.A: Transmission of knowledge and skills
options.B: Development of capabilities
options.C: Formation of peer networks and social relationships
options.D: Allocation of people to occupational positions

questions.explanation: A latent function is an unintended or unrecognised consequence. The formation of peer networks and social relationships through education is often an unintended consequence, whereas transmission of knowledge, development of capabilities and occupational allocation are manifest functions.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a manifest function of education?

options.A: Formation of peer networks
options.B: Transmission of knowledge and skills

questions.explanation: A manifest function is an intended and recognised consequence. The transmission of knowledge and skills is an intended and recognised function of education.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a function of the family?

options.A: Reproduction
options.B: Socialisation

questions.explanation: The family performs reproduction, socialisation, care, emotional support, regulation of sexual relations and transmission of culture. Conducting elections is a political function, not a family function.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of affinal kinship?

options.A: Parent-child relationship
options.B: Sibling relationship

questions.explanation: Affinal kinship refers to relationships created through marriage, such as relationships between spouses and in-laws. Parent-child, sibling and grandparent-grandchild relationships are consanguineal kinship.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of consanguineal kinship?

options.A: Relationship between spouses
options.B: Relationship between in-laws
options.D: Relationship between a couple and their children's spouses

questions.explanation: Consanguineal kinship refers to relationships understood as arising through descent, such as parent-child and sibling relationships.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: A group that an individual uses as a standard for evaluating their own attitudes and behaviour is called what?

options.A: In-group
options.B: Out-group

questions.explanation: A reference group is a group that an individual uses as a standard for evaluating attitudes, behaviour, values or aspirations.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: A group with which a person identifies and feels a sense of belonging is called what?

options.A: Out-group
options.B: In-group

questions.explanation: An in-group is a group with which a person identifies and to which the person feels a sense of belonging.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: A group that a person perceives as outside their own group is called what?

options.A: In-group
options.B: Out-group

questions.explanation: An out-group is a group that a person perceives as outside their own group, sometimes with feelings of distance or opposition.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: Which of the following is the correct order of the four varnas in classical Hindu textual traditions?

options.A: Kshatriya, Brahmana, Vaishya, Shudra
options.B: Brahmana, Kshatriya, Vaishya, Shudra

questions.explanation: Varna is a broad fourfold classification found in classical Hindu textual traditions: Brahmana, Kshatriya, Vaishya and Shudra.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: In Marxist analysis, the class that owns or controls the means of production is called what?

options.A: Proletariat
options.B: Bourgeoisie

questions.explanation: In Marxist analysis, the bourgeoisie or capitalist class owns or controls the means of production.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: In Marxist analysis, the class of wage workers who do not own the means of production is called what?

options.A: Bourgeoisie
options.B: Proletariat

questions.explanation: In Marxist analysis, the proletariat is the class of wage workers who do not own the means of production and sell their labour power.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: In Weber's analysis, a group distinguished by social honour, prestige and lifestyle is called what?

options.A: Class
options.B: Status group

questions.explanation: In Weber's analysis, a status group is a group distinguished by social honour, prestige, lifestyle or recognised standing.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: In Weber's analysis, organised groups seeking to influence or exercise power are called what?

options.A: Class
options.B: Status group

questions.explanation: In Weber's analysis, party refers to organised groups seeking to influence or exercise power, especially in political or organisational settings.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a common basis of class?

options.A: Income
options.B: Wealth

questions.explanation: Common bases of class include income, wealth, occupation, education, ownership of productive assets, market position and lifestyle. Caste endogamy is a feature of caste, not class.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: The process by which a group becomes more similar to another group through the adoption of cultural patterns is called what?

options.A: Cultural diffusion
options.B: Acculturation

questions.explanation: Assimilation is a process in which a group becomes more similar to another group through the adoption of cultural patterns, potentially reducing distinct cultural differences.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: Cultural change that occurs when groups maintain sustained contact and adopt or adapt elements of one another's cultures is called what?

options.A: Cultural lag
options.B: Acculturation

questions.explanation: Acculturation is cultural change that occurs when groups maintain sustained contact and adopt or adapt elements of one another's cultures.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a characteristic of the Panchayati Raj system?

options.A: It is a system of rural local self-government
options.B: It is constitutionally recognised through Part IX of the Constitution
options.C: It was given constitutional status by the 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992
options.D: It is a system of urban local government

questions.explanation: Panchayati Raj is the system of rural local self-government in India, constitutionally recognised through Part IX of the Constitution and given constitutional status by the 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992. Urban local government is a separate system under Part IX-A.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a civil marriage law in India?

options.A: The Hindu Marriage Act, 1955
options.B: The Special Marriage Act, 1954
options.C: The Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, 2006
options.D: The Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955

questions.explanation: The Special Marriage Act, 1954 is an Indian law providing a civil form of marriage for persons irrespective of religion, subject to the Act's legal conditions and procedures.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a constitutional provision related to caste?

options.A: Article 14 guarantees equality before the law
options.B: Article 15 prohibits discrimination on grounds including caste
options.C: Article 16 provides equality of opportunity in public employment
options.D: Article 32 provides for the abolition of caste

questions.explanation: Article 32 provides for the right to constitutional remedies, not the abolition of caste. Article 17 abolishes untouchability; Articles 14, 15 and 16 relate to equality and non-discrimination.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a social dysfunction?

options.A: An institution successfully meeting a social need
options.B: An institution creating difficulties or undermining the functioning of a social system
options.C: An intended consequence of an institution
options.D: A recognised function of an institution

questions.explanation: A social dysfunction is a consequence of a social arrangement that creates difficulties or undermines the functioning of a social system.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT an agent of socialisation?

options.A: Family
options.B: Peer group

questions.explanation: Major agents of socialisation include family, peer groups, schools, religion, mass media, workplace, community and digital media. A biological instinct is not a socialisation agent.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of accommodation?

options.A: Two groups working together for a common goal
options.B: Two conflicting groups adjusting to reduce disagreement and enable continued interaction
options.C: Two groups competing for limited resources
options.D: One group adopting the culture of another

questions.explanation: Accommodation is the adjustment of conflicting individuals or groups to reduce or manage disagreement and enable continued interaction.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of assimilation?

options.A: Two groups competing for resources
options.B: Two conflicting groups adjusting to reduce disagreement
options.C: A group gradually adopting elements of another culture and developing shared cultural patterns
options.D: Two groups working together for a common goal

questions.explanation: Assimilation is a process through which individuals or groups gradually adopt elements of another culture and develop shared cultural patterns.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of intersectionality?

options.A: Studying caste in isolation
options.B: Examining how caste, class and gender interact to shape distinct experiences of advantage and disadvantage

questions.explanation: Intersectionality is an approach that examines how social categories such as caste, class, gender and ethnicity can interact to shape distinct experiences of advantage and disadvantage.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: A family formed when partners establish a family unit that includes children from previous relationships is called what?

options.A: Nuclear family
options.B: Joint family

questions.explanation: A blended or reconstituted family is formed when partners establish a family unit that includes children from one or both partners' previous relationships.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a social movement?

options.A: A temporary gathering of people
options.B: A sustained collective effort by people seeking to promote, resist or reverse social change

questions.explanation: A social movement is a sustained collective effort by people seeking to promote, resist or reverse social change.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a slum?

options.A: A planned residential area with adequate housing
options.B: A densely populated urban area with inadequate housing and poor sanitation

questions.explanation: A slum is a densely populated urban settlement or area characterised by inadequate housing and one or more forms of deprivation, such as insecure tenure, poor sanitation or insufficient basic services.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a factor promoting social mobility?

options.A: Education
options.B: Industrialisation

questions.explanation: Inherited wealth is a barrier to social mobility, not a factor promoting it. Factors promoting social mobility include education, occupational change, industrialisation, urbanisation, economic growth, migration, technological change, public policy and social reform.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: The Gram Sabha consists of which of the following?

options.A: Elected representatives only
options.B: Government officials only
options.C: Persons registered in the electoral rolls relating to a village within the area of a Gram Panchayat

questions.explanation: The Gram Sabha consists of persons registered in the electoral rolls relating to a village within the area of a Gram Panchayat.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of secularisation?

options.A: Increasing influence of religious institutions in politics
options.B: Reduced role or authority of religious institutions in certain areas of social life
options.C: Adoption of religious practices by a caste group
options.D: Spread of religious ideas from one society to another

questions.explanation: Secularisation refers to changes in which religious institutions, beliefs or practices have a reduced role or authority in certain areas of social life.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: Is sociology only the study of social problems?

options.A: Yes, sociology only studies social problems
options.B: No, sociology scientifically studies society, social relationships, social institutions, social interaction, social processes, social structures and social change

questions.explanation: No. Sociology scientifically studies society, social relationships, social institutions, social interaction, social processes, social structures and social change.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: Who chaired the Drafting Committee of the Indian Constitution?

options.A: Jawaharlal Nehru
options.B: Dr. B. R. Ambedkar

questions.explanation: Dr. B. R. Ambedkar chaired the Drafting Committee of the Indian Constitution.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of institutionalisation?

options.A: Building a new school
options.B: Repeated practices and rules becoming established, accepted and relatively stable patterns of social life

questions.explanation: Institutionalisation is the process through which repeated practices and rules become established, accepted and relatively stable patterns of social life.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of an arranged marriage?

options.A: A marriage in which the prospective spouses primarily choose each other based on their relationship
options.B: A marriage in which families or intermediaries play a significant role in identifying or negotiating a match
options.C: A marriage registered under state law

questions.explanation: An arranged marriage is one in which families or intermediaries play a significant role in identifying or negotiating a match; the degree of individual choice varies.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: A group that develops through personal relationships and spontaneous interaction rather than a formally prescribed structure is called what?

options.A: Formal group
options.B: Informal group

questions.explanation: An informal group develops through personal relationships and spontaneous interaction rather than a formally prescribed structure.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: A group with deliberately established rules, roles, procedures and objectives is called what?

options.A: Informal group
options.B: Formal group

questions.explanation: A formal group has deliberately established rules, roles, procedures and objectives.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: A group that individuals join by choice is called what?

options.A: Involuntary group
options.B: Voluntary group

questions.explanation: A voluntary group is one that individuals join by choice, such as a cultural association or charitable organisation.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: A group into which membership is assigned or into which a person is born is called what?

options.A: Voluntary group
options.B: Involuntary group

questions.explanation: An involuntary group is one into which membership is assigned or into which a person is born, such as a family of birth.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of caste mobility?

options.A: A caste group's social position remaining completely unchanged over time
options.B: Changes in the social position or status claims of caste groups over time through education, economic change, political organisation and cultural change
options.C: The process of marrying within one's caste
options.D: The practice of hereditary service relationships

questions.explanation: Caste mobility refers to changes in the social position or status claims of caste groups over time, through processes such as education, economic change, political organisation and cultural change.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a status group in Weber's analysis?

options.A: A group defined by its relationship to the means of production
options.B: A group distinguished by social honour, prestige and lifestyle
options.C: A group seeking to influence political power
options.D: A group based on caste endogamy

questions.explanation: In Weber's analysis, a status group is a group distinguished by social honour, prestige, lifestyle or recognised standing.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of community development?

options.A: A government programme imposed without local participation
options.B: A participatory process through which people collectively identify needs, mobilise resources and improve their community

questions.explanation: Community development is a participatory process through which people collectively identify needs, mobilise resources and improve their community.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a peasant movement?

options.A: A movement by workers to improve wages and working conditions
options.B: Collective action by cultivators or rural people around issues such as land, rent, wages, debt, rights or agrarian policy
options.C: A movement seeking fundamental transformation of the political order
options.D: A movement seeking to change particular laws while retaining the broader system

questions.explanation: A peasant movement is collective action by cultivators or rural people around issues such as land, rent, wages, debt, rights or agrarian policy.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a labour movement?

options.A: Collective action by cultivators around land issues
options.B: Organised collective action by workers to improve wages, working conditions, rights and social protection
options.C: A movement seeking fundamental transformation of the political order
options.D: A movement seeking to change particular laws while retaining the broader system

questions.explanation: A labour movement is organised collective action by workers to improve wages, working conditions, rights and social protection.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of cooperation?

options.A: Two groups competing for limited resources
options.B: Two individuals or groups working together to achieve a common goal
options.C: Two groups in deliberate opposition over values
options.D: One group adopting the culture of another

questions.explanation: Cooperation is a process in which individuals or groups work together to achieve a common goal.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of competition?

options.A: Two groups working together for a common goal
options.B: Two individuals or groups seeking a limited resource, reward or position that cannot be obtained by all
options.C: Two groups in deliberate opposition over power
options.D: One group adopting the culture of another

questions.explanation: Competition is a social process in which individuals or groups seek a limited resource, reward or position that cannot be obtained by all.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of conflict?

options.A: Two groups working together for a common goal
options.B: Two groups seeking a limited resource
options.C: Deliberate opposition or struggle between individuals or groups over interests, values, power or resources
options.D: One group adopting the culture of another

questions.explanation: Conflict is a social process involving deliberate opposition or struggle between individuals or groups over interests, values, power or resources.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a manifest function of religion?

options.A: Unintended reinforcement of social hierarchies
options.B: Providing systems of beliefs and practices concerning the sacred and offering moral guidance

questions.explanation: A manifest function is an intended and recognised consequence. Providing systems of beliefs and practices concerning the sacred and offering moral guidance is an intended and recognised function of religion.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a latent function of religion?

options.A: Providing moral guidance
options.B: Creating collective identity
options.C: Unintended reinforcement of social solidarity through communal gatherings
options.D: Offering meaning and social solidarity as recognised goals

questions.explanation: A latent function is an unintended or unrecognised consequence. Unintended reinforcement of social solidarity through communal gatherings can be a latent function of religion.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of family disorganisation?

options.A: A family functioning smoothly with shared roles
options.B: Disruption in family relationships, roles or functioning arising from conflict, separation, violence or economic stress
options.C: A family expanding into a joint family
options.D: A family migrating to a new place

questions.explanation: Family disorganisation refers to disruption in family relationships, roles or functioning, which may arise from conflict, separation, violence, economic stress or other causes.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of bilateral descent?

options.A: Tracing descent only through the male line
options.B: Tracing descent only through the female line
options.C: Recognising kinship through both the mother's and the father's lines

questions.explanation: Bilateral descent recognises kinship through both the mother's and the father's lines.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a closed system of stratification?

options.A: A system where education and achievement permit movement between positions
options.B: A caste system where status is assigned largely by birth
options.C: A class system with high mobility
options.D: A system with no social positions

questions.explanation: A closed system restricts movement between social positions and assigns status largely by birth or inherited membership, as in a caste system.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of an open system of stratification?

options.A: A caste system where status is assigned by birth
options.B: A class system where education and achievement permit movement between positions
options.C: A system with no social positions
options.D: A system where movement between positions is completely restricted

questions.explanation: An open system permits comparatively greater movement between social positions, often through education, occupation, income or achievement, as in a class system.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of rural-to-urban migration?

options.A: A person moving from a city to a village
options.B: A person moving from a village to a city in search of employment
options.C: A person moving from one city to another
options.D: A person moving from one country to another

questions.explanation: Rural-to-urban migration is the movement of people from villages or rural areas to towns and cities.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of the jajmani system?

options.A: A system of caste endogamy
options.B: A traditional arrangement of hereditary, reciprocal service and exchange relationships between landholding households and service-providing groups in some Indian villages

questions.explanation: The jajmani system was a traditional arrangement of hereditary, reciprocal service and exchange relationships between cultivating or landholding households and service-providing groups in some Indian villages.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of untouchability?

options.A: A discriminatory practice historically imposed on communities considered polluting or socially excluded
options.B: A form of caste endogamy
options.C: A system of hereditary service relationships
options.D: A process of upward social mobility

questions.explanation: Untouchability is a discriminatory practice historically imposed on communities considered polluting or socially excluded; it is prohibited under Article 17 of the Constitution of India.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of class consciousness?

options.A: Awareness among members of a class of their shared position, interests and relationship with other classes
options.B: The consciousness of the upper class only

questions.explanation: Class consciousness is awareness among members of a class of their shared position, interests and relationship with other classes.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of modernisation?

options.A: A society undergoing industrialisation, urbanisation, scientific and technological development, bureaucratisation and expansion of formal education
options.B: A society adopting only Western dress
options.C: A society focusing only on rural development
options.D: A society experiencing only cultural diffusion

questions.explanation: Modernisation is a broad process of transformation involving changes such as industrialisation, urbanisation, scientific and technological development, bureaucratisation and expansion of formal education.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of globalisation?

options.A: A village isolated from all external contact
options.B: The intensification of cross-border flows and connections involving goods, services, capital, people, information, technology and culture
options.C: A society focusing only on local production
options.D: A society rejecting all foreign influence

questions.explanation: Globalisation is the intensification of cross-border flows and connections involving goods, services, capital, people, information, technology and culture.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a social structure?

options.A: A temporary crowd at a festival
options.B: The relatively stable, organised pattern of social relationships, statuses, roles, groups and institutions in society

questions.explanation: Social structure is the relatively stable, organised pattern of social relationships, statuses, roles, groups and institutions in society.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of primary socialisation?

options.A: Learning roles and expectations in a workplace
options.B: Learning language and basic norms within the family during early childhood
options.C: Learning the values of a profession one expects to enter

questions.explanation: Primary socialisation is the early and foundational learning of language, basic norms, values and behaviour, commonly within the family.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of secondary socialisation?

options.A: Learning language from parents in early childhood
options.B: Learning basic norms within the family
options.C: Learning roles and expectations in schools, workplaces and peer groups

questions.explanation: Secondary socialisation is the learning of roles and expectations in settings beyond the early family environment, such as schools, workplaces and peer groups.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of monogamy?

options.A: A man having more than one wife at the same time
options.B: A woman having more than one husband at the same time
options.C: A person having one spouse at a time

questions.explanation: Monogamy is a marriage form in which a person has one spouse at a time.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of polygyny?

options.A: A woman having more than one husband at the same time
options.B: A man having more than one wife at the same time
options.C: A person having one spouse at a time

questions.explanation: Polygyny is a form of polygamy in which one man has more than one wife.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of polyandry?

options.A: A man having more than one wife at the same time
options.B: A woman having more than one husband at the same time
options.C: A person having one spouse at a time

questions.explanation: Polyandry is a form of polygamy in which one woman has more than one husband.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of community sentiment?

options.A: A legal document forming a community
options.B: The feeling of belonging, attachment and shared identity among members of a community
options.D: An economic transaction within a community

questions.explanation: Community sentiment is the feeling of belonging, attachment and shared identity among members of a community.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a virtual community?

options.A: A village community
options.B: A group whose members interact and develop shared interests or identity primarily through digital communication platforms

questions.explanation: A virtual community is a group whose members interact and develop shared interests or identity primarily through digital communication platforms.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a social value?

options.A: A personal preference for a particular food
options.B: A shared belief that honesty is important in society

questions.explanation: A social value is a shared belief about what is desirable, important or worthwhile in a society, such as the importance of honesty.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a social norm?

options.A: A personal opinion about music
options.B: A shared expectation that people should queue in line at a ticket counter

questions.explanation: A social norm is a shared rule or expectation that guides behaviour in a particular society or group, such as queuing in line.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of the economic institution?

options.A: A system of beliefs concerning the sacred
options.B: The organisation of production, distribution, exchange and consumption of goods and services
options.C: The organisation of power and authority
options.D: The transmission of knowledge and skills

questions.explanation: The economic institution organises production, distribution, exchange and consumption of goods and services.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of political institutions?

options.A: A system of beliefs concerning the sacred
options.B: The organisation of production and consumption
options.C: The organisation of power, authority, governance, collective decision-making and the maintenance of public order
options.D: The transmission of knowledge and skills

questions.explanation: Political institutions organise power, authority, governance, collective decision-making and the maintenance of public order.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a matriarchal family?

options.A: A family in which authority and decision-making are predominantly vested in men
options.B: A family system in which women, especially mothers, hold predominant authority
options.C: A family that traces descent through the father's line
options.D: A family where the couple lives with the husband's family

questions.explanation: A matriarchal family is a family system in which women, especially mothers, hold predominant authority.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a patriarchal family?

options.A: A family in which women hold predominant authority
options.B: A family in which authority and decision-making are predominantly vested in men, especially senior men
options.C: A family that traces descent through the mother's line
options.D: A family where the couple lives with the wife's family

questions.explanation: A patriarchal family is one in which authority and decision-making are predominantly vested in men, especially senior men.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a lineage?

options.A: A descent group whose members claim descent from a legendary ancestor whose exact identity is unknown
options.B: A descent group whose members trace their relationship to a known common ancestor
options.C: A group formed through marriage only

questions.explanation: A lineage is a descent group whose members trace their relationship to a known common ancestor.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a clan?

options.A: A descent group whose members trace their relationship to a known common ancestor
options.B: A descent group whose members claim descent from a common ancestor, who may be legendary or not individually known
options.C: A group formed through marriage only

questions.explanation: A clan is a descent group whose members claim descent from a common ancestor, who may be legendary or not individually known.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a dominant caste?

options.A: A caste that is numerically the smallest and has no economic resources
options.B: A caste that exercises substantial local influence through numerical strength, landownership, economic resources, political power and social status
options.C: A caste that is excluded from society
options.D: A caste that has no political power

questions.explanation: A dominant caste is a caste that exercises substantial local influence through a combination of numerical strength, landownership, economic resources, political power and social status.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of social inequality?

options.A: Equal distribution of resources among all people
options.B: Unequal distribution of resources, opportunities, rights, power or rewards among individuals and groups

questions.explanation: Social inequality refers to unequal distribution of resources, opportunities, rights, power or rewards among individuals and groups.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of urban planning?

options.A: Unplanned growth of a city
options.B: The process of organising land use, housing, transport, infrastructure, public spaces and services to guide urban development
options.C: The movement of people from cities to villages

questions.explanation: Urban planning is the process of organising land use, housing, transport, infrastructure, public spaces and services to guide urban development.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of rural development?

options.A: The process of urbanisation
options.B: The process of improving rural livelihoods, infrastructure, education, healthcare, employment, participation and overall quality of life
options.D: The process of migration to cities

questions.explanation: Rural development is the process of improving rural livelihoods, infrastructure, education, healthcare, employment, participation and overall quality of life.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of social progress?

options.A: Any change in society regardless of its direction
options.B: Change judged as improvement according to specified values, such as equality, welfare, freedom, health or education

questions.explanation: Social progress is change judged as improvement according to specified values, such as equality, welfare, freedom, health or education; not every social change is necessarily progress.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of social development?

options.A: Any change in social structure
options.B: Planned or measurable improvement in people's well-being, capabilities, institutions and access to opportunities

questions.explanation: Social development is planned or measurable improvement in people's well-being, capabilities, institutions and access to opportunities.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: Which of the following is a characteristic of social interaction?

options.A: It involves individuals acting and reacting in relation to one another
options.B: It involves only physical movement

questions.explanation: Social interaction is the process through which individuals act and react in relation to one another.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: Which of the following is a characteristic of social institutions?

options.A: They are temporary and short-lived
options.B: They are organised, relatively enduring, governed by norms and values, involve statuses and roles, meet social needs, and are transmitted across generations
options.C: They are based purely on individual choice
options.D: They have no connection to social needs

questions.explanation: Social institutions are organised, relatively enduring, governed by norms and values, involve statuses and roles, meet social needs, and are transmitted across generations.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: Which of the following is a characteristic of a primary group?

options.A: Impersonal and goal-oriented relationships
options.B: Intimate, personal, face-to-face and enduring relationships

questions.explanation: A primary group is a relatively small group characterised by intimate, personal, face-to-face and enduring relationships.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: Which of the following is a characteristic of a secondary group?

options.A: Intimate and personal relationships
options.B: Generally larger and more formal, with relationships that are often impersonal, specialised and goal-oriented

questions.explanation: A secondary group is generally larger and more formal, with relationships that are often impersonal, specialised and goal-oriented.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: Which of the following is a constitutional provision related to caste?

options.A: Article 17 abolishes untouchability
options.B: Article 32 abolishes caste

questions.explanation: Article 17 of the Constitution of India abolishes untouchability and forbids its practice in any form.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: Which of the following is a constitutional provision related to equality?

options.A: Article 14 guarantees equality before the law and equal protection of the laws
options.B: Article 32 guarantees equality before the law
options.C: Article 368 guarantees equality before the law
options.D: Article 280 guarantees equality before the law

questions.explanation: Article 14 of the Constitution of India guarantees equality before the law and equal protection of the laws.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: Which of the following is a constitutional provision prohibiting discrimination?

options.A: Article 15 prohibits discrimination on grounds including religion, race, caste, sex and place of birth
options.B: Article 32 prohibits discrimination

questions.explanation: Article 15 of the Constitution of India prohibits discrimination on grounds including religion, race, caste, sex and place of birth.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: Which of the following is a constitutional provision providing equality of opportunity in public employment?

options.A: Article 14
options.B: Article 15

questions.explanation: Article 16 of the Constitution of India provides equality of opportunity in matters of public employment.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: Which of the following is a constitutional provision directing the State to promote the interests of weaker sections?

options.A: Article 14
options.B: Article 15
options.D: Article 46, a Directive Principle of State Policy

questions.explanation: Article 46, a Directive Principle of State Policy, directs the State to promote the educational and economic interests of weaker sections, particularly Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: Which of the following is a law governing marriage among persons to whom the Hindu Marriage Act applies?

options.A: The Special Marriage Act, 1954
options.B: The Hindu Marriage Act, 1955
options.C: The Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, 2006
options.D: The Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955

questions.explanation: The Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 is an Indian law governing marriage among persons to whom the Act applies, including provisions concerning conditions for a valid marriage, ceremonies, restitution, judicial separation, divorce and related matters.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: Which of the following is a law providing a civil form of marriage for persons irrespective of religion?

options.A: The Hindu Marriage Act, 1955
options.B: The Special Marriage Act, 1954
options.C: The Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, 2006
options.D: The Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955

questions.explanation: The Special Marriage Act, 1954 is an Indian law providing a civil form of marriage for persons irrespective of religion, subject to the Act's legal conditions and procedures.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: Which of the following is a law intended to prohibit child marriages and provide legal remedies and penalties?

options.A: The Hindu Marriage Act, 1955
options.B: The Special Marriage Act, 1954
options.C: The Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, 2006
options.D: The Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955

questions.explanation: The Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, 2006 is an Indian law intended to prohibit child marriages and provide legal remedies and penalties.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: Which of the following is a law that makes the practice of untouchability punishable?

options.A: The Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955, which was originally enacted as the Untouchability (Offences) Act, 1955
options.B: The Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989
options.C: The Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, 2006

questions.explanation: The Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955, which was originally enacted as the Untouchability (Offences) Act, 1955, makes the practice of untouchability punishable.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: Which of the following is a law that addresses atrocities against members of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes?

options.A: The Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955
options.B: The Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989
options.C: The Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, 2006

questions.explanation: The Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 addresses atrocities against members of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: Which of the following is a constitutional provision related to Panchayats?

options.A: Part IX, Articles 243 to 243O
options.B: Part IX-A, Articles 243P to 243ZG

questions.explanation: Part IX, Articles 243 to 243O of the Constitution of India contains the provisions on Panchayats.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: Which of the following is a constitutional provision related to Municipalities?

options.A: Part IX, Articles 243 to 243O
options.B: Part IX-A, Articles 243P to 243ZG

questions.explanation: Part IX-A, Articles 243P to 243ZG of the Constitution of India contains the provisions on Municipalities, added by the 74th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of cultural diffusion?

options.A: The delay in adjusting laws to new technology
options.B: The spread of a new farming technique from one society to another
options.C: The process of adopting another culture completely

questions.explanation: Cultural diffusion is the spread of cultural traits, ideas, practices or technologies from one group or society to another.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of cultural lag?

options.A: The spread of a new technology from one society to another
options.B: The delay in adjusting laws and values to rapid technological change
options.C: The process of adopting another culture completely

questions.explanation: Cultural lag is the delay in the adjustment of one part of culture, often non-material culture such as laws or values, to changes in another part, often technology.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of accommodation in society?

options.A: Two groups working together for a common goal
options.B: Two conflicting groups reaching a compromise to enable continued interaction
options.C: Two groups competing for limited resources
options.D: One group adopting the culture of another

questions.explanation: Accommodation is the adjustment of conflicting individuals or groups to reduce or manage disagreement and enable continued interaction.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of the functionalist explanation of stratification?

options.A: Stratification is unnecessary and should be abolished
options.B: Stratification helps ensure that important positions are filled by suitably trained people through unequal rewards
options.C: Stratification is based purely on class conflict
options.D: Stratification is based on caste endogamy

questions.explanation: Davis and Moore argued that stratification helps ensure that important positions are filled by suitably trained people through unequal rewards; this thesis has been widely criticised.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: What is the basic format used throughout the Sociology chapter?

options.A: A complete question or statement followed immediately by a direct, exam-oriented answer
options.B: Only multiple-choice questions

questions.explanation: The chapter uses a complete question or statement followed immediately by a direct, exam-oriented answer.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: What should a candidate remember when studying sociological definitions?

options.A: All sociologists define concepts in exactly the same way
options.B: Different sociologists sometimes define the same concept differently; learn the central idea and associate a named definition with the correct scholar
options.C: Definitions are not important for exams
options.D: Only one definition per concept is correct

questions.explanation: Different sociologists sometimes define the same concept differently. Learn the central idea and associate a named definition with the correct scholar.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a reform movement?

options.A: A movement seeking fundamental and rapid transformation of the political order
options.B: A movement seeking to change particular laws or practices while generally retaining the broader social system
options.C: A movement by cultivators around land issues
options.D: A movement by workers to improve wages

questions.explanation: A reform movement seeks to change particular institutions, laws or practices while generally retaining the broader social system.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a revolutionary movement?

options.A: A movement seeking to change particular laws while retaining the broader social system
options.B: A movement seeking fundamental and often rapid transformation of the political, economic or social order
options.C: A movement by cultivators around land issues
options.D: A movement by workers to improve wages

questions.explanation: A revolutionary movement seeks fundamental and often rapid transformation of the political, economic or social order.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a major basis of social stratification?

options.A: Class
options.B: Caste

questions.explanation: Class, caste, gender, race or ethnicity, occupation, wealth, power, education and status can shape social stratification. Blood group is a biological characteristic, not a major basis of social stratification.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a major social institution?

options.A: Family
options.B: Marriage

questions.explanation: The family, marriage, kinship, education, religion, economy, polity or government, and law are commonly treated as major social institutions. A cricket team is an organisation, not a major social institution.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT an essential feature of a social group?

options.A: Interaction
options.B: Mutual awareness

questions.explanation: Essential features of a social group include interaction, mutual awareness, shared norms or interests, a sense of belonging, and some degree of organisation or continuity. Physical proximity alone is not sufficient.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a common characteristic historically associated with caste?

options.A: Birth-based membership
options.B: Endogamy

questions.explanation: Common characteristics historically associated with caste include birth-based membership, endogamy, hierarchy, hereditary or traditionally associated occupations, social restrictions and ideas of purity and pollution. Free mobility between groups is not a characteristic of caste.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a major factor promoting social mobility?

options.A: Education
options.B: Industrialisation

questions.explanation: Social exclusion is a barrier to social mobility, not a factor promoting it. Factors promoting social mobility include education, occupational change, industrialisation, urbanisation, economic growth, migration, technological change, public policy and social reform.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a major cause of urbanisation?

options.A: Industrialisation
options.B: Employment opportunities

questions.explanation: Major causes of urbanisation include industrialisation, employment opportunities, migration, expansion of services, education, transport, administrative growth and natural increase of urban populations. A decrease in urban population would be the opposite of urbanisation.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a common challenge faced by rural society?

options.A: Agrarian distress
options.B: Unequal land distribution

questions.explanation: Common challenges faced by rural society include agrarian distress, unequal land distribution, unemployment or underemployment, limited infrastructure, inadequate services, social discrimination, migration and environmental vulnerability. Excessive employment opportunities is not a common challenge.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a major source of social change?

options.A: Technology
options.B: Economy

questions.explanation: Major sources of social change include technology, economy, population change, environment, cultural diffusion, education, political action, social movements, conflict and changes in values. Complete isolation from external contact would tend to reduce some sources of change.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a main characteristic of social stratification?

options.A: It is socially structured
options.B: It is hierarchical

questions.explanation: Social stratification is socially structured, hierarchical, relatively persistent, involves unequal rewards and opportunities, and varies across societies and historical periods. It is not temporary and random.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a major agent of socialisation?

options.A: Family
options.B: Peer groups

questions.explanation: Major agents of socialisation include family, peer groups, schools, religion, mass media, workplace, community and digital media. A person's blood group is a biological characteristic, not a socialisation agent.

questions.subject: Sociology
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a main characteristic of a community?

options.A: A sense of belonging
options.B: Social interaction

questions.explanation: A community commonly involves a sense of belonging, social interaction, shared interests or identity, continuity and some form of common life. Complete absence of continuity is not a characteristic of a community.
